# Wait for a rendered Email inbox before the scroll witness

## Context
[Brain-tier CI on the repaired Pipeline PR](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42313343415/job/128220201527) failed `test/playwright/e2e/realworld/EmailMultiWindowNL.spec.mjs:61`: the first row stayed at index 0 after a native wheel event. The frozen `initial.rowPool` was also 0; 16 other shard tests passed. The original trace is [artifact 13550386508](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42313343415/artifacts/13550386508).

## The Problem
The witness admits `rowPool < storeCount`, which accepts an empty pool (`0 < 250`). It therefore can dispatch its one wheel event before the grid is rendered/scrollable. Even a later index greater than zero would not prove scrolling beyond an established buffered pool. This is a test-readiness defect; the receipt alone does not establish a grid-product regression or a Pipeline cause.

## The Architectural Reality
At `f7a2afe6f6`, `openEmail` waits for workspace visibility, while `grid.Body#createViewData` (825) returns until rows, width and column positions exist. Body items initially form an empty pool. Email's `store/Emails.mjs` supplies local Model-backed data, with no Pipeline configuration. `grid.View.scrollTop` and the native `.neo-grid-view` scrollport provide separate scroll observations.
Design authority: #6600's intake contract requires “Browser scroll beyond the initial pool” and selected-record/detail agreement. An empty baseline cannot prove that contract.

## The Fix
Repair the existing Email E2E witness. Await a positive bounded worker row pool, a visible initial row, and positive scrollable native geometry before freezing its baseline or sending native input. Target the actual scrollport. Retain the existing beyond-pool row-index and selected-email/detail assertions, and keep a failure distinguishable as readiness, native scrolling, or row synchronization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A zero row pool cannot become the frozen scroll baseline. The ready pool is positive and smaller than the known Store population.
- [ ] Native wheel input follows visible initial rows and a scrollport whose scroll height exceeds its positive client height. No fixed sleep or relaxed row-index threshold substitutes for readiness.
- [ ] A bounded delayed-layout/readiness control demonstrates that input waits; once released, native scrolling reaches beyond the frozen initial pool. Preserve native and worker/painted-row observations so a product regression still fails.
- [ ] All four existing Email multi-window journeys pass, including same-instance reader returns, retained draft editing, source-close behavior and independent popup returns. Preserve their current assertions and record the runtime used.

## Out of Scope
No Email or Grid behavior/API changes, Pipeline changes, test quarantine, weakened popup/identity assertions, Bridge retirement, or shared harness timing policy.

## Avoided Traps
A longer timeout cannot make an already-dispatched early wheel valid. Repeating wheels inside a polling assertion hides the readiness boundary. Replacing the frozen pool with a later pool weakens the original witness.

Related: #6600, #20447, #20487. #4548's visibility repair is separate and remains delivered.
